title: Preserving Disagreement: Architectural Heterogeneity and Coherence Validation in Multi-Agent Policy Simulation

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating artificial consensus, sycophancy, and 'debate capture' by calculating the first-choice concentration metric to measure how frequently LLM agents abandon their assigned viewpoints to agree with the majority during multi-agent debate.

Comparing convergence rates between homogeneous multi-agent systems (using a single base model) and heterogeneous systems (using different models) to isolate spurious agreement caused by shared training data and RLHF preferences.

Assigning distinct normative value perspectives (e.g., Security Focus, Risk Tolerance, Pragmatism) to LLM agents and using a coherence validation layer to measure if the models can faithfully maintain diverse policy positions rather than defaulting to a single preferred policy.

Rewriting policy option descriptions in a child welfare scenario to be symmetrically appealing to test whether initial description asymmetry (description bias) drives agent convergence, as detailed in the rebalanced scenario test.
